objective: A frozen exploratory census, exact: every connected map of up to five contacts (rotation systems on any surface, no contact joining a ring to itself), as networks of equally spaced rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts, and every contact of it: whether it persists, and whether it has a flip; any contact that persists without a flip is listed.
status: Closed: refuted 2026-11-09 (exploratory, exact; frozen contracts pre-registered in 7581ed1fa and b28d92b98): a contact can persist without a flip. E001: every map to five contacts read exhaustively; exceptions from three contacts, all degenerate (a contact that sends or hears nothing, or a ring or face of one or two contacts). E002: on random non-degenerate maps of six to nine contacts most persistent contacts have no flip (17,992 of 21,056 at six), many of them sending and hearing; the smallest has six contacts on genus 2, its returns even at every length with no symmetry.
title: Persistence without a flip: a search of small maps
